q: During an outage of the central authentication service, a badge-controlled server room falls back to denying all entry until service is restored. Which secure design principle does this illustrate?
c: Fail securely
Least privilege
Separation of duties
Defense in depth

q: A vendor distributes firmware updates through public mirrors and must let devices confirm that each image is authentic and unmodified before installation. Which mechanism BEST meets this requirement?
c: A digital signature over each firmware image
A SHA-256 hash published beside each image
An HMAC computed with a shared device key
TLS encryption for every download session

q: A military system must prevent users from reading documents classified above their clearance level. Which security model directly enforces this 'no read up' rule?
c: Bell-LaPadula
Biba
Clark-Wilson
Brewer-Nash

q: A privileged installer checks a file's permissions, and an attacker swaps the file for a symbolic link in the instant between that check and the privileged write. Which vulnerability class is being exploited?
c: A buffer overflow in the installer
An insecure direct object reference
A time-of-check to time-of-use race condition
A privilege escalation via DLL injection

q: Researchers recover an encryption key from a smart card by passively measuring fluctuations in its power consumption during cryptographic operations. Which attack class does this represent?
c: A chosen-plaintext attack
A side-channel attack
A brute-force attack
A fault-injection attack

q: A data center wants to stop an unauthorized person from slipping through a secure entrance behind an employee's single badge swipe. Which physical control BEST addresses this?
c: CCTV cameras covering the entrance
Additional badge readers on interior doors
Security awareness posters at the door
A mantrap with interlocking doors

q: A laptop fleet must release its disk encryption keys only when each machine boots with untampered firmware and boot loader. Which hardware capability provides this?
c: A Trusted Platform Module measuring the boot chain
A hardware security module in the data center
Self-encrypting drives with drive-lock passwords
UEFI passwords protecting the firmware menu

q: During an architecture review, a security engineer finds that a company's flat internal network relies entirely on a single perimeter firewall; any host that gets past it can reach every server, including the payroll database. Which secure design principle is MOST directly violated by this architecture?
c: Least privilege, because internal users hold more access rights than their jobs require
Separation of duties, because one firewall team controls all security decisions
Defense in depth, because a single control failure exposes every internal asset
Open design, because the security of the network depends on keeping its layout secret

q: A financial data platform ingests unverified market feeds at a low integrity level and maintains an audited general ledger at a high integrity level. The architect wants a formal model rule that stops processes handling the unverified feeds from writing into the ledger. Which rule provides this?
c: The Biba *-integrity axiom, which forbids a subject from writing to objects at a higher integrity level
The Biba simple integrity axiom, which forbids a subject from reading objects at a lower integrity level
The Bell-LaPadula *-property, which forbids a subject from writing to objects at a lower sensitivity level
The Clark-Wilson certification rules, which require auditors to certify every transformation procedure

q: A consulting firm serves two competing banks. Management wants an access control model in which a consultant who opens documents belonging to one bank is dynamically barred from accessing the competitor's data for as long as the conflict exists. Which model is designed for this requirement?
c: Bell-LaPadula, which restricts access based on hierarchical sensitivity labels and clearances
Graham-Denning, which defines rules for securely creating and transferring access rights
Biba, which restricts access based on hierarchical integrity levels assigned to subjects and objects
Brewer-Nash, which changes a subject's permissible objects based on its access history

q: An architect designing a payment system requires that users can never modify account balance records directly; every change must go through certified programs that validate the transaction, and the duty to initiate and approve transfers is split between roles. Which security model formalizes these requirements?
c: Bell-LaPadula, which mediates access using security labels and mandatory access rules
Clark-Wilson, which binds users to data through certified transformation procedures
Biba, which prevents subjects from reading down or writing up across integrity levels
Take-Grant, which models how access rights can be passed between subjects and objects

q: A security manager must select controls for a new internal scheduling application rated low impact for confidentiality, integrity, and availability. A junior engineer proposes applying every control in the organization's master catalog 'to be safe.' What is the MOST appropriate response?
c: Approve the proposal, since applying the full catalog guarantees the system cannot be under-protected
Reject the proposal and let the development team choose whichever controls they consider practical
Select the baseline matching the system's impact level, then tailor it to the system's environment and risks
Defer control selection until a penetration test of the finished system identifies the weaknesses to address

q: A procurement team is comparing two firewalls. Product A is certified at EAL4 against a network device Protection Profile; Product B claims EAL2. A manager concludes that Product A 'is twice as secure.' Which statement BEST corrects this interpretation?
c: A higher EAL means the product's security claims were evaluated with greater rigor, not that the product offers stronger protection
A higher EAL means the product includes more security functions, so Product A does provide broader protection than Product B
EAL ratings apply only to government systems, so the comparison is irrelevant for a commercial procurement decision
EAL ratings measure resistance to penetration testing, so Product A withstood roughly twice the attack effort of Product B

q: A payments company must ensure that the private keys used to sign transactions can never be read by server administrators or exported in cleartext, even if the host operating system is fully compromised. Which capability BEST meets this requirement?
c: Storing the keys in an encrypted software keystore protected by a strong passphrase
Generating and using the keys inside a hardware security module that never releases them
Splitting the keys among administrators using an m-of-n secret-sharing arrangement
Recording the keys in a sealed envelope kept in a bank safe-deposit box for recovery

q: After a faulty third-party device driver repeatedly crashed an entire operating system, an architect redesigns the platform so drivers run as unprivileged user-mode processes communicating with a small kernel. Which security capability is the architect PRIMARILY applying?
c: Trusted platform module attestation, which verifies the integrity of code before it is loaded
Data execution prevention, which stops the processor from executing writable memory pages
Full-disk encryption, which protects the confidentiality of the driver binaries stored at rest
Process isolation with reduced privilege, which confines faults so a failing driver cannot take down the kernel

q: A company adopts a SaaS HR platform. Months later, an audit finds that ex-employees still hold active accounts and that sensitive reports are shared through public links. The IT director argues the SaaS provider is accountable for these findings. Which response BEST reflects the cloud shared responsibility model?
c: The customer remains responsible for identity lifecycle and data-sharing configuration even in SaaS, so these findings belong to the company
The provider is responsible because in SaaS the vendor manages the application layer, which includes all account and sharing settings
Responsibility transfers to the provider once the contract includes a security addendum covering confidentiality of customer data
Both findings are the provider's fault because public link sharing is a platform design flaw rather than a customer configuration choice

q: A virtualization team plans to consolidate internet-facing DMZ virtual machines and internal database servers onto the same hypervisor cluster to cut hardware costs. The CISO objects to the design. Which risk MOST directly justifies the objection?
c: VM sprawl will increase because a consolidated cluster makes it easier to create unmanaged virtual machines
Live migration of guests between hosts will move workloads without updating the configuration management database
A guest-escape or hypervisor compromise from an exposed DMZ workload would place attackers adjacent to the most sensitive systems
Resource contention between database and web workloads will degrade performance during traffic peaks

q: A water utility's PLCs run firmware that the vendor no longer updates, and a vulnerability scanner flags critical CVEs against them. The devices cannot be replaced for three years. Which mitigation BEST addresses the risk in the interim?
c: Schedule monthly authenticated vulnerability scans of the PLCs to track whether the exposures worsen over time
Isolate the PLC network behind strict segmentation with tightly controlled, monitored conduits to the business network
Deploy host-based antivirus agents to each PLC to detect malware attempting to exploit the known flaws
Purchase cyber insurance sized to the estimated impact of a successful attack on the treatment process

q: During a design review of a new order-processing platform, an architect notices that every microservice authenticates to the database with the same account, which has full read-write access to all schemas, because it 'simplifies deployment.' Which secure design principle should the reviewer cite FIRST?
c: Fail securely, because a database outage would leave every service in an undefined state
Complete mediation, because the database should recheck authorization on every query
Defense in depth, because a single firewall should not be the only control protecting the database
Least privilege, because each service should hold only the minimum access its function requires

q: An engineer asks why a TLS connection uses asymmetric cryptography only briefly at the start of a session and then switches to a symmetric cipher for the remainder. What is the PRIMARY reason for this hybrid design?
c: Symmetric ciphers are far faster for bulk data, while asymmetric methods solve the key distribution problem during setup
Asymmetric ciphers are more secure, so they are reserved for protecting the most sensitive part of the exchange
Symmetric ciphers provide non-repudiation, which is required for the application data but not for the handshake
Asymmetric keys wear out after limited use, so sessions must switch to symmetric keys before that limit is reached

q: A developer encrypts millions of customer records with AES, but a reviewer notices that identical plaintext fields always produce identical ciphertext blocks, letting analysts infer which customers share attributes. Which change BEST resolves this weakness?
c: Increase the AES key length from 128 to 256 bits so the ciphertext becomes harder to brute force
Hash each field with SHA-256 before encryption so identical values no longer look alike
Use an authenticated mode such as AES-GCM with a unique nonce per record instead of ECB mode
Encrypt each record twice with two different AES keys to double the effective security margin

q: A CISO is told that future quantum computers may break the public-key algorithms protecting the company's long-retention data, and that standardized post-quantum algorithms are now available. What should the organization do FIRST?
c: Replace all TLS certificates immediately with certificates using post-quantum signature algorithms
Build an inventory of where and how cryptography is used across systems, protocols, and data retention periods
Increase all RSA key sizes to 8192 bits to extend protection until the migration is complete
Suspend encryption of archival data until the post-quantum migration plan has been approved

q: To guarantee business continuity, a compliance officer proposes escrowing copies of every private key in the enterprise PKI, including employees' digital signature keys, in a corporate key-recovery system. What is the MOST significant problem with this proposal?
c: Escrowed keys expire on the same schedule as operational keys, so the archive provides no continuity benefit
Key-recovery systems can only store symmetric keys, so the PKI's asymmetric keys cannot be escrowed
Escrow doubles certificate issuance costs because each escrowed key requires a second certificate
Escrowing signature keys destroys non-repudiation, since signers can claim another party had access to their key

q: A legal team signs contract hashes computed with an outdated hash function. An insider prepares two contracts with different payment terms that produce the same hash, obtains a signature on the harmless version, and later substitutes the other. Which attack does this describe, and what property failed?
c: A birthday attack exploiting the hash function's inadequate collision resistance
A preimage attack exploiting the ability to recover the original document from its hash
A replay attack exploiting reuse of a previously captured signature in a new session
A chosen-ciphertext attack exploiting decryption of attacker-supplied messages

q: After a breach, forensics shows attackers recovered most user passwords from stolen unsalted MD5 hashes within hours by using precomputed tables. Which change would have been MOST effective at defeating this specific technique?
c: Requiring users to choose passwords of at least ten characters with mixed character classes
Encrypting the password database with AES using a key stored in the application configuration
Hashing each password with a unique random salt using a slow, memory-hard password hashing function
Locking accounts after five failed login attempts to slow online guessing against the system

q: Analysts notice that a man-in-the-middle can tamper with a client's protocol negotiation so that both endpoints, though capable of a modern cipher suite, settle on a legacy export-grade suite the attacker can break offline. Which cryptanalytic technique is being used?
c: A meet-in-the-middle attack that trades memory for time against a double-encryption construction
A downgrade attack that forces negotiation of weaker parameters the attacker can then defeat
A side-channel attack that infers keys from timing variations in the handshake computations
A related-key attack that exploits mathematical relationships between the session keys

q: A researcher testing an encrypted messaging gateway can submit arbitrary messages of her choosing and capture the resulting ciphertexts, which she analyzes to deduce information about the encryption key. Under which cryptanalytic attack model is she working?
c: Ciphertext-only, because she ultimately works from captured ciphertext to find the key
Known-plaintext, because she knows the content of the messages that were encrypted
Chosen-ciphertext, because she chooses which captured ciphertexts to analyze in depth
Chosen-plaintext, because she selects the inputs the system encrypts and studies the outputs

q: A campus redesign adds low trimmed hedges, wide clear sightlines from lobby desks to every entrance, and pedestrian paths routed past occupied offices. Which crime-prevention concept do these choices PRIMARILY apply?
c: Natural surveillance, which increases the likelihood that intruders are observed by legitimate occupants
Natural access control, which uses layout to channel people through defined entry points
Territorial reinforcement, which uses design cues to signal that a space is owned and cared for
Target hardening, which strengthens physical barriers so that forced entry takes longer

q: A facilities engineer must specify sprinkler protection for a new data hall. Leadership fears an accidental discharge destroying equipment, but the fire code still requires water-based suppression. Which system BEST balances these concerns?
c: A wet pipe system, because water is always at the head and discharges the instant any head fuses
A deluge system, because all heads release simultaneously to overwhelm a fast-growing fire
A pre-action system, because pipes stay dry until detection and a fused head both occur before water flows
A dry pipe system alone, because compressed air in the pipes eliminates any chance of accidental water release

q: A data center design specifies that the HVAC system must maintain positive air pressurization within the server rooms relative to surrounding corridors. What is the PRIMARY purpose of this requirement?
c: It lowers energy costs by reducing the volume of air that must be recirculated and cooled
It forces air to flow outward when doors open, keeping dust and contaminants from entering
It raises humidity levels enough to prevent static discharge from damaging server components
It slows the spread of fire by starving the flames of oxygen inside the pressurized rooms

q: An ERP system critical to manufacturing runs on an operating system whose vendor ended all support last month; no more security patches will ever be issued. Replacement is budgeted for eighteen months out. What is the security manager's BEST course of action?
c: Continue normal operations, since the system has run without incident and replacement is already funded
Immediately shut the system down until the replacement platform is ready for production use
Rely on the annual penetration test to reveal whether the unsupported platform is actually exploitable
Document the risk for formal acceptance by the owner and apply compensating controls such as isolation and monitoring until migration

q: A CIO asks when in the information system lifecycle security requirements should FIRST be defined in order to minimize both risk and rework cost. What is the BEST answer?
c: During system testing, when security flaws can be found and fixed before release
During operations and maintenance, when real-world threats to the system are finally known
During initiation and requirements definition, before the architecture is designed
During disposal planning, so data destruction obligations can shape the system's design

q: A fintech startup's lead developer proposes protecting transaction data with an in-house cipher whose internal design will be kept strictly secret, arguing that attackers cannot break what they cannot study. Which secure design principle BEST explains why the security architect should reject this proposal?
c: Defense in depth, because a single secret algorithm represents only one layer of protection
Least privilege, because too many developers would eventually learn the algorithm's design
Open design, because the system's security should rest on protected keys, not on keeping the mechanism itself secret
Economy of mechanism, because a custom algorithm adds unnecessary complexity to the platform

q: A SaaS provider learns that one tenant received query results belonging to another tenant. Investigation shows all tenants share a single in-memory cache service that keys entries by query text alone, so identical queries from different tenants can return the same cached entry. Which secure design principle was MOST directly violated?
c: Least privilege, because the cache service was granted access to more data than any single tenant required
Least common mechanism, because a component shared across tenants became a path for data to cross trust boundaries
Fail securely, because the caching fault should have produced a denial of service instead of a disclosure
Complete mediation, because the platform should have re-validated authorization on every cache lookup

q: A network appliance vendor is defining the factory configuration its product will ship with. Which approach BEST reflects the principle of secure defaults?
c: Ship with nonessential services disabled and require administrators to explicitly enable the features they need
Ship with all features enabled so administrators can disable whatever their environment does not require
Ship with a common documented password so initial setup is simple, then prompt for hardening later
Ship with an optional wizard that recommends hardening steps the administrator may apply after installation

q: An evaluator is concerned that on a multilevel system, processes at a lower classification could infer what higher-level processes are doing by observing changes in response times and resource availability, even though no explicit read of protected data ever occurs. Which security model MOST directly addresses this concern?
c: Bell-LaPadula, because its simple security property forbids lower-level subjects from reading higher-level data
Clark-Wilson, because well-formed transactions would prevent the lower-level processes from observing the system
Brewer-Nash, because it dynamically restricts access once a subject has observed related information
Noninterference, because it requires that higher-level activity have no observable effect on what lower-level subjects can see

q: A security architect wants to determine whether a specific access right could ever propagate to an unauthorized subject in a collaboration platform. She models subjects and objects as nodes in a directed graph and applies rules describing how rights may be taken from or granted to other nodes. Which formal model is she applying?
c: Graham-Denning, which defines eight protection rules for securely creating and deleting subjects, objects, and rights
Bell-LaPadula, which determines whether information can flow between sensitivity levels
Harrison-Ruzzo-Ullman, which analyzes commands that modify an access control matrix
Take-Grant, which uses graph rewriting rules to decide whether a right can reach a given subject

q: A regulation requires encryption at rest for a claims database, but the legacy application cannot support it, the vendor offers no fix, and replacement is two years away. What is the security manager's BEST course of action?
c: Formally accept the risk and note that encryption will arrive with the replacement platform
Direct the project team to replace the legacy system immediately, regardless of the migration schedule
Implement and document compensating controls of equivalent protection, such as strict access restriction and enhanced monitoring of the database
Transfer the regulatory exposure by purchasing a cyber liability insurance policy for the system

q: A procurement specification contains two statements: the product must enforce role-based access control, and the vendor must supply independent evaluation evidence demonstrating the mechanism was built and tested correctly. How are these requirements BEST characterized?
c: The first is a functional security requirement and the second is an assurance requirement
Both are functional requirements, because each one concerns the access control mechanism
The first is an assurance requirement and the second is a functional requirement
The first is a technical control and the second is an administrative control

q: To improve performance, an operating system vendor proposes caching access-control decisions so repeated requests by a process for the same file bypass the security kernel after the first check. Sessions can last for days, and file permissions in the environment change frequently. Which reference monitor property does the proposal MOST endanger?
c: Verifiability, because the caching logic would make the kernel too large to be formally analyzed
Complete mediation, because revoked permissions would not take effect while stale cached decisions are still honored
Tamperproofness, because a decision cache held in kernel memory could be altered by unprivileged processes
Economy of mechanism, because the cache introduces a second, redundant authorization code path

q: A security engineer wants platform capabilities that make it harder for an attacker to execute shellcode injected through a stack buffer overflow in a running application. Which combination BEST addresses this goal?
c: Full-disk encryption combined with pre-boot authentication of the user
Non-executable memory protection combined with address space layout randomization
File integrity monitoring combined with signed application installers
A host-based firewall combined with strict outbound traffic filtering

q: A laptop standard requires that a machine refuse to start the operating system at all if its bootloader has been modified, rather than merely recording the modification for later review. Which capability satisfies this requirement?
c: Measured boot, which extends a hash of each boot component into platform configuration registers
Full-disk encryption, which prevents an attacker from reading or altering the bootloader offline
Secure Boot, which verifies digital signatures on boot components and halts the process when verification fails
Remote attestation, which lets a management server evaluate the platform's recorded boot measurements

q: For the third time in a year, a development team has exposed sensitive files by setting a cloud object-storage bucket to public. Leadership asks for a response that prevents recurrence across the whole organization. Which action is BEST?
c: Enforce organization-wide guardrail policies that block public bucket access by default and require documented exceptions
Enroll all developers in additional security awareness training on cloud data handling
Encrypt all bucket contents at rest using the provider's managed encryption keys
Schedule quarterly penetration tests focused on discovering publicly exposed storage

q: On a multilevel system, evaluators find that a process holding classified material alternately creates and deletes a file in a world-readable spool directory, while an uncleared process polls for the file's existence and interprets the pattern as binary data. What is this mechanism MOST accurately called?
c: A covert timing channel, because the uncleared process must poll on a schedule to read the signal
A side-channel attack, because information leaks through a mechanism never intended for communication
An inference attack, because the uncleared process derives protected information it was never given
A covert storage channel, because information is signaled by modulating an observable attribute of a shared resource

q: A product security review finds that every unit of a shipping smart-sensor product line uses the same administrative password embedded in firmware, and field data shows customers almost never change it. Which remediation BEST addresses the underlying weakness?
c: Publish installation guidance strongly urging customers to change the password during setup
Provision unique per-device credentials during manufacturing and force credential setup before first use
Obfuscate the firmware image so the embedded password cannot be extracted by analysis
Require TLS on the management interface so the password cannot be captured in transit

q: A review of a container platform finds that once traffic is inside the cluster, any microservice can call any other service's API; only connections arriving from the internet are authenticated at the gateway. Which change BEST mitigates the risk posed by a single compromised service?
c: Deploy a more capable web application firewall in front of the internet-facing gateway
Consolidate the services onto a single hardened host to reduce the network attack surface
Require mutual TLS with per-service identities so every service authenticates its callers before serving requests
Terminate TLS at the gateway and re-encrypt the traffic on its way to backend services

q: Investigators confirm that an attacker who stole a web server's long-term private key had also been recording the site's encrypted traffic for months. Management asks the architect to ensure a future key theft cannot expose previously captured sessions. Which property should the TLS configuration provide?
c: Forward secrecy, using ephemeral key agreement so session keys cannot be derived from the server's long-term key
Key escrow, so an independent third party retains protected copies of the session keys
Certificate pinning, so clients reject any certificate other than the one they expect
A longer server key, so recorded traffic cannot be factored within a useful timeframe

q: A payment processor is designing the generation ceremony for its root key-encrypting key. The stated requirement is that no single employee should ever be able to reconstruct or use the key alone. Which arrangement BEST satisfies the requirement?
c: Store the complete key in a safe under the sole custody of the most senior security officer
Subject the designated key custodian to an enhanced background check and a signed nondisclosure agreement
Keep two identical copies of the full key with two different officers in separate locations
Divide the key into components held by separate custodians and require a quorum of them to reconstitute it

q: Two companies authenticate settlement files exchanged between them using an HMAC computed with a single shared secret key. A dispute arises in which Company A alleges that Company B fabricated a file and its authentication tag. Which statement BEST explains why the HMAC cannot settle the dispute?
c: HMAC provides only confidentiality, so the origin of the file was never protected
Either company could have computed a valid tag with the shared key, so the tag cannot prove which party created the file
HMAC tags are vulnerable to collision attacks that let outside parties forge files at will
The shared key was not rotated frequently enough to preserve the evidentiary value of the tags

q: A web application decrypts a CBC-mode encrypted cookie and returns one error message when the padding is invalid and a different one when padding is valid but the content fails a check. An attacker submits thousands of systematically modified cookies, using each response to construct the next attempt, and recovers the plaintext. Which attack model does this exemplify?
c: An adaptive chosen-ciphertext attack, because crafted ciphertexts are submitted and each response guides the next submission
A ciphertext-only attack, because the attacker began with nothing but an encrypted cookie
A known-plaintext attack, because the differing error messages disclose fragments of the plaintext
An exhaustive key search, because thousands of attempts were required to complete the recovery

q: A vendor proposes strengthening a legacy 56-bit block cipher by encrypting each block twice with two independently chosen keys and markets the result as having 112 bits of effective strength. Which cryptanalytic technique MOST directly undermines this claim?
c: A birthday attack, which finds matching outputs after roughly the square root of the keyspace is searched
A related-key attack, which exploits mathematical relationships between the two encryption keys
A meet-in-the-middle attack, which trades memory for time to reduce the effective strength to little more than one encryption
Frequency analysis, which exploits statistical patterns that survive both encryption passes

q: A telemetry radio protocol uses a stream cipher, but after every device reboot the transmitter restarts encryption with the same key and the same initialization vector. An analyst XORs two captured post-reboot transmissions together and begins recovering both messages. Which flaw enables the recovery?
c: The cipher's key is too short, allowing the analyst to exhaust the keyspace
The protocol omits message authentication, allowing transmissions to be modified undetected
The initialization vector is sent in the clear, allowing the analyst to read the keystream
Keystream reuse: encrypting two messages with the same key and IV lets their XOR cancel the keystream entirely

q: A company evaluating land for a new data center finds the least expensive parcel lies within a mapped flood plain and borders a rail line regularly used by chemical tank cars. What is the BEST recommendation from a security architecture perspective?
c: Acquire the parcel and transfer the hazard exposure through comprehensive property insurance
Acquire the parcel and elevate all critical equipment above the projected flood level
Reject the parcel, because site selection is the cheapest point at which to avoid hazards later controls cannot fully offset
Acquire the parcel and plan a fully equipped disaster recovery site in another region

q: A physical security assessment of a headquarters building on a busy urban street recommends protecting the lobby entrance and the queue of people outside it from an accidental or deliberate vehicle strike. Which control BEST addresses this specific threat?
c: Continuous CCTV coverage of the street approach with monitoring by the security operations center
Crash-rated bollards establishing standoff distance between the roadway and the entrance
Uniformed guards posted outside the entrance during business hours
Full-height turnstiles controlling pedestrian access just inside the lobby

q: While specifying electronic locks for a data center's emergency exits, the design team debates how the doors should behave during a fire alarm or total power loss. Which approach is BEST?
c: Configure egress doors to unlock on alarm or power loss, and compensate with local alarms and camera coverage on those doors
Configure the doors to remain locked during incidents so the equipment inside cannot be stolen amid the confusion
Require a guard in the operations center to remotely release the doors when an evacuation is confirmed
Keep the doors fail-secure and stage break-glass override keys at the main security desk

q: A company must select fire suppression for a continuously staffed network operations bridge that shares space with critical IT equipment. The system must be able to discharge without endangering the staff on duty or destroying the electronics. Which option is BEST?
c: A carbon dioxide total-flooding system with automatic discharge on detection
A wet-pipe sprinkler system fed from the building's main fire loop
A dry-chemical powder system positioned above the equipment racks
A clean-agent gaseous system approved for use in occupied spaces

q: Servers leased for three years processed confidential client data and are now due to be returned to the leasing company. What is the BEST requirement for the security team to impose before the hardware leaves the facility?
c: Delete all data volumes and reformat each drive using the operating system's standard tools
Sanitize each drive with a method matched to its media type and data sensitivity, then verify and document the results
Rely on the leasing company's contractual commitment to wipe all returned equipment
Remove and physically shred every drive before returning the remaining hardware

q: After the security team mandates 16-character passwords rotated every 30 days on a legacy system with no single sign-on, help-desk reset tickets triple and auditors find passwords written on monitors and saved in shared spreadsheets. Which secure design principle did the control design MOST clearly violate?
c: Psychological acceptability, because controls that impose excessive burden push users into insecure workarounds
Least privilege, because users were granted more access rights than their job duties actually require
Fail securely, because the system does not default to a protective state when an error occurs
Separation of duties, because one person can both request a password reset and approve it

q: A security architect reviews a proposal that lets any device on the corporate LAN reach internal applications directly because "the perimeter firewall keeps attackers out." Which design approach BEST addresses the architect's concern about this assumption?
c: Tighten perimeter firewall rules so only approved ports and protocols can reach the internal applications
Adopt a zero trust approach that authenticates and authorizes every request regardless of where on the network it originates
Deploy honeypots on the internal LAN so that any attacker who breaches the perimeter is quickly detected
Require full-disk encryption on every endpoint that is permitted to connect to the corporate LAN

q: During design of a customer loyalty application, the product team proposes collecting birth dates, government ID numbers, and continuous location history because the data "might be useful later." Which response by the security architect BEST reflects privacy by design?
c: Approve collection but require strong encryption of every sensitive field at rest and in transit
Approve collection provided customers accept a consent checkbox describing all data uses at signup
Limit collection to the fields required for defined loyalty functions and set retention limits before development begins
Approve collection but require the analytics team to de-identify the data before running any reports

q: An analyst working in a session cleared at Secret attempts to save a document into an Unclassified shared folder, and the mandatory access control system blocks the write. Which Bell-LaPadula rule caused the denial?
c: The simple security property, which prevents subjects from reading objects above their clearance level
The discretionary security property, which enforces need-to-know through an access matrix
The simple integrity axiom, which prevents subjects from reading data at lower integrity levels
The star (*) property, which prevents subjects from writing to objects below their security level

q: An operating system design team needs a formal basis for how subjects and objects are securely created and deleted, and how access rights are granted, transferred, and revoked between them. Which security model MOST directly defines this set of eight primitive protection operations?
c: The Graham-Denning model
The Bell-LaPadula model
The Harrison-Ruzzo-Ullman model
The Take-Grant model

q: A military logistics system must both prevent disclosure of classified shipment data and ensure inventory records are modified only by validated processes. The architect observes that no single classic lattice model satisfies both goals. Which approach BEST meets the requirement?
c: Apply Bell-LaPadula alone, since preventing unauthorized reads also prevents unauthorized modification of records
Combine confidentiality and integrity lattices in the style of Lipner's implementation, layering Bell-LaPadula levels with Biba-style integrity categories
Apply Brewer-Nash so that each user's permitted accesses adjust dynamically based on what they have previously read
Apply the noninterference model so that actions at high levels cannot influence what lower-level subjects observe

q: A new HR platform will process benefits enrollment data rated low impact, payroll data rated moderate, and executive disciplinary records rated high for confidentiality impact. When selecting the initial security control baseline, how should the overall system be categorized?
c: At moderate, because that reflects the average of the impact ratings across the information types
With a separate baseline applied individually to each information type within the system
At high, because overall categorization follows the highest impact level among the information types it processes
At low, and raised later only if an incident demonstrates that the impact was underestimated

q: A security engineer proposes a $250,000 hardware-based data loss prevention platform to protect a public marketing asset library that contains no sensitive data and would cost under $20,000 to fully re-create. What is the BEST reason for the risk manager to reject the proposal?
c: The proposed platform has not been evaluated and certified under the Common Criteria
Hardware-based controls are inherently less flexible and effective than administrative controls
Data loss prevention addresses only confidentiality, while integrity should always take priority
The cost of the safeguard is grossly disproportionate to the value and risk exposure of the asset

q: A mobile payments application must match the user's fingerprint template on the device in a way that prevents even a fully compromised operating system kernel from reading the template or tampering with the match decision. Which platform capability BEST meets this requirement?
c: A trusted execution environment that runs the matching code and holds the template in a hardware-isolated enclave outside the main OS
Full-disk encryption bound to the user's passcode so that the stored template is protected whenever the device is powered off
Storing the template inside a kernel-mode driver whose memory locations are randomized by address space layout randomization
Hashing the template with a salted, memory-hard algorithm before storage so the raw biometric is never kept on the device

q: Users of shared workstations report having typed their credentials into what was later found to be a malicious full-screen replica of the login window drawn by malware. Which operating system capability is specifically designed to defeat this attack?
c: Address space layout randomization applied to the login process and its libraries
A trusted path invoked by a secure attention sequence that guarantees credentials reach only the genuine operating system login handler
Application sandboxing that prevents each program from reading the memory of other running processes
An encrypted credential vault that automatically fills stored passwords into login forms

q: In a multilevel logistics database, users cleared at Unclassified have learned that whenever a vessel's destination row is missing or locked, a classified mission is underway — the absence of data itself leaks information. Which database mechanism BEST mitigates this inference channel?
c: Encrypting the classified rows so that lower-cleared users cannot decrypt the destination values
Auditing and throttling queries from lower-cleared users to detect repeated probing of vessel records
Polyinstantiation, storing different tuples for the same vessel at different classification levels so lower-cleared users see a plausible cover record
Content-dependent views that remove the classified destination column from lower-cleared users' results

q: A DevOps team pulls container base images directly from public registries into production builds. A review finds several deployed images contained cryptominers and severely outdated libraries. Which control approach BEST addresses this architectural weakness?
c: Harden the container host operating systems to an industry benchmark and restrict shell access to them
Deploy runtime antimalware agents that scan the filesystem inside every running production container
Apply egress filtering on the production network so cryptominer traffic to external pools is blocked
Require images to come from a curated internal registry, verify image signatures, and scan images before promotion

q: A defense contractor processing highly classified material is concerned that an adversary leasing the adjacent office suite could reconstruct screen contents and keystrokes from electromagnetic emanations leaking through the shared wall. Which mitigation MOST directly addresses this threat?
c: Shielded enclosures, filtered power, and emanation-security (TEMPEST-style) zoning that keeps radiating equipment at controlled distances from uncontrolled space
Encrypting all classified data with AES-256 both at rest on workstations and in transit across the internal network
Installing acoustic white-noise masking systems along the shared wall and in nearby conference rooms
Enforcing a strict clean-desk policy and fitting polarized privacy filters to every monitor in the suite

q: An audit of a virtualization cluster discovers dozens of undocumented virtual machines created by developers over several years; several run unpatched operating systems with routes into production networks. Which action should the security team take FIRST?
c: Delete every undocumented virtual machine immediately to eliminate the unmanaged attack surface
Inventory all discovered VMs, assign owners, and bring each under configuration and lifecycle management before remediating or retiring them
Deploy a hypervisor-integrated intrusion prevention sensor to monitor east-west traffic among the virtual machines
Revoke developers' self-service VM creation rights so that no further unmanaged machines can appear

q: After a web server's private key is stolen, a bank revokes its TLS certificate, yet clients keep accepting the old certificate for days: they refresh CRLs weekly and treat revocation-lookup failures as success. Which change BEST reduces the exposure window for revoked certificates?
c: Publish the CRL to additional mirror distribution points so client downloads fail less often
Reissue the replacement certificate with a much longer RSA key so the new private key cannot be stolen
Have servers staple current OCSP responses into the TLS handshake and move toward short-lived certificates
Pin the replacement certificate's public key inside the bank's client applications

q: A design team must add strong public-key authentication to battery-powered field sensors that have minimal processing power, memory, and energy budgets. Which cryptographic choice BEST fits these constraints?
c: RSA with 4096-bit keys to provide the largest possible security margin on each sensor
AES-256 used as the authentication mechanism since symmetric ciphers are computationally cheap
SHA-256 hashing of each device's serial number transmitted as its authentication proof
Elliptic curve cryptography, which achieves comparable security to RSA with far smaller keys and lower computational cost

q: A data platform has encrypted everything with the same AES key for six years, accumulating petabytes of ciphertext. The security architect insists on defining a cryptoperiod and rotating keys. What is the PRIMARY risk the rotation policy addresses?
c: The volume of data and time of exposure under a single key keep growing, magnifying the impact of a key compromise and enlarging the material available for cryptanalysis
AES keys mathematically degrade with age, so encryption strength weakens the longer any single key remains in service
Extended use makes brute-force recovery of the key statistically certain to succeed within the key's lifetime
Periodic rotation is required to keep the encryption module's FIPS 140 validation from lapsing

q: A developer protects exported support tickets by consistently replacing each letter of the alphabet with a different fixed letter. A security analyst warns that any such scheme can be broken within minutes. Which cryptanalytic technique does the analyst have in mind?
c: A birthday attack that finds two tickets producing the same output value
Frequency analysis, which exploits the characteristic letter and word frequencies that a monoalphabetic substitution preserves
A meet-in-the-middle attack that works inward from both the input and the output
A padding oracle attack that decrypts the text by observing error responses

q: Researchers show that briefly dropping the supply voltage of a set-top box CPU at one precise instant causes the boot ROM's signature verification branch to be skipped, allowing unsigned firmware to execute. Which attack class does this demonstrate?
c: Differential power analysis recovering the signature verification key from consumption traces
A downgrade attack forcing the device to negotiate a weaker, breakable verification algorithm
A fault injection attack that induces a hardware error at a chosen moment to bypass a security check
A time-of-check to time-of-use race condition between the verification and the execution of the firmware

q: While preparing a long-term cryptographic roadmap, an architect must brief leadership on how large-scale quantum computers would affect the algorithms in use today. Which statement is MOST accurate?
c: Quantum computers threaten symmetric and asymmetric algorithms equally, so every algorithm in the estate must be replaced at the same time
Only key-exchange protocols are affected, so data encrypted with AES-128 needs no attention in quantum planning
Doubling RSA moduli to 8192 bits restores an adequate security margin against quantum factoring
Shor's algorithm breaks RSA and elliptic curve cryptography outright, while Grover's only halves effective symmetric strength, so AES-256 remains adequate

q: An architect reviewing floor plans finds the new server room placed on the ground floor against an exterior wall with a window, directly beneath a floor of restrooms served by pressurized water lines. Which recommendation BEST reflects secure facility design?
c: Relocate the room to a windowless interior space on a middle floor, away from plumbing runs, exterior walls, and flood-prone levels
Keep the location but fit reinforced glazing over the window and aim a monitored camera at the exterior wall
Keep the location but install a raised floor with under-floor moisture sensors and drip pans beneath the ceiling penetrations
Move the server room to the top floor of the building so it is farthest from street-level threats and any site flooding

q: A campus redesign uses walkway placement, landscaping, low fencing, and gate positioning so that visitors are naturally guided toward a single staffed lobby entrance, while routes toward service doors feel clearly off-limits and awkward to take. Which CPTED concept is being applied?
c: Natural surveillance, because the design increases the ability of occupants to observe visitors
Natural access control, because the physical layout channels people toward authorized entry points and away from unauthorized ones
Territorial reinforcement, because the design signals the boundary between public and private ownership
Maintenance and image, because a well-kept environment discourages offenders from testing the site

q: During a utility outage, a data center's diesel generator started as designed but needed 45 seconds to reach stable output. Every server crashed the instant utility power failed. Which element of the power protection design was missing or undersized?
c: An automatic transfer switch capable of sensing the outage and switching the load to the generator
Surge protectors and line conditioners to smooth the incoming utility power feed
An online UPS with battery capacity sized to carry the full load through the gap until generator output stabilizes
A second utility feed delivered from a different substation to eliminate single-provider dependence

q: A new insurance claims system has completed independent security assessment. Several moderate residual risks cannot be remediated before the contractual go-live date. Who should decide whether the system may enter operation, and on what basis?
c: The information system security officer, based on whether every planned control passed its test
The independent assessor, based on the findings documented in the security assessment report
The development project manager, based on the contractual commitments and the delivery schedule
A senior authorizing official, based on a formal decision to accept the residual risk on behalf of the organization

q: After a system goes live, the project team disbands and all security activities cease; no vulnerability scans or control assessments are scheduled because "the system already passed its authorization." Which recommendation by the security manager BEST addresses this gap?
c: Establish continuous monitoring for the operations phase: scheduled scanning, ongoing control assessments, and reauthorization triggers for significant changes
Schedule a complete reaccreditation of the system every year regardless of whether anything about it has changed
Rely on the security operations center's incident detection capability to surface any weaknesses that emerge in production
Commission a repeat of the original penetration test to confirm that the authorized baseline is still intact

q: An architect must choose between two designs for a session-validation component: one with a single, well-understood token verification path, and one offering pluggable validators, dynamic policy scripting, and legacy fallback modes. Both meet the functional requirements. Which secure design principle MOST strongly favors the first design?
c: Defense in depth, because the simpler design layers fewer controls that can conflict
Least privilege, because fewer features means fewer permissions must be granted
Economy of mechanism, because a small, simple design is easier to verify and has fewer flaws
Open design, because a simpler component is easier to publish for public review

q: A development team has completed the high-level design for a new payments API and wants to identify spoofing, tampering, and information-disclosure threats before any code is written. Which activity BEST accomplishes this at this stage of the project?
c: Conduct structured threat modeling of the design using a methodology such as STRIDE
Schedule a penetration test of the completed application prior to its release
Run static application security testing tools against the source code repository
Perform an authenticated vulnerability scan of the staging environment servers

q: Several internal applications connect directly to a core banking database and issue ad hoc SQL, exposing schema details and unrelated columns to every client team. The architect replaces direct access with a service API that exposes only a small set of approved operations and hides the underlying structure. Which design principle is the architect PRIMARILY applying?
c: Least common mechanism, by removing components that multiple applications share
Abstraction with information hiding, by exposing only necessary operations and concealing internal detail
Separation of duties, by dividing database work among multiple application teams
Complete mediation, by rechecking authorization on every individual data request

q: A build server designated as high integrity automatically ingests configuration snippets posted to a public, unmoderated wiki designated as low integrity, and incorporates them into production build scripts. Under the Biba model, which rule does this data flow violate?
c: The *-integrity axiom, which prevents a subject from writing to objects of higher integrity
The simple security property, which prevents a subject from reading above its clearance level
The strong star property, which restricts subjects to reading and writing only at their own level
The simple integrity axiom, which prevents a high-integrity subject from reading lower-integrity data

q: A security engineer explains that a formally verified operating system is proven to start in a secure state and that every permitted transition leads only to another secure state, so the system can never enter an insecure condition. Which foundational model does this describe?
c: The information flow model, which tracks how data moves between objects at different levels
The state machine model, which proves security is preserved across all states and transitions
The noninterference model, which ensures high-level actions are invisible to low-level subjects
The Take-Grant model, which uses a directed graph to analyze how rights can be transferred

q: A researcher wants to reason formally about whether a discretionary access control system could ever leak a specific right to an unauthorized subject, given commands that create subjects and objects and modify cells of an access matrix. Which model addresses this question, and what is its central finding?
c: Harrison-Ruzzo-Ullman, which shows that deciding whether a right can leak is undecidable in the general case
Graham-Denning, which proves its eight primitive protection operations always keep rights from leaking
Bell-LaPadula, which proves the star property prevents any propagation of rights between subjects
Clark-Wilson, which shows well-formed transactions guarantee that access rights can never escape

q: An agency applying a moderate control baseline to an industrial control system finds that several baseline controls are unsuitable for the operational technology environment, while sector-specific risks the baseline never anticipated remain unaddressed. What is the BEST mechanism for adapting the control set?
c: Document formal risk acceptance for every baseline control that does not fit the environment
Escalate the system to the high baseline so that all potentially needed controls are included
Apply a published overlay that adds, removes, and adjusts baseline controls for that specialized operating environment
Replace the control catalog with the vendor hardening guides supplied for each ICS component

q: A control baseline assigned to an air-gapped system includes several requirements for protecting wireless access, but the facility prohibits wireless technology and the system contains no radio hardware. The security team documents that these controls do not apply and records the justification. Which tailoring activity does this represent?
c: Selecting compensating controls to substitute for safeguards that cannot be implemented
Applying a control overlay designed for systems operating in specialized environments
Supplementing the baseline with additional controls to cover environment-specific risks
Scoping out controls whose underlying conditions are absent from the system's environment

q: An operating system runs its kernel with unrestricted access to privileged CPU instructions, while applications execute at a lower privilege level and must request kernel services through controlled system-call interfaces. Which hardware security capability enables this separation?
c: Processor protection rings that enforce hierarchical privilege levels for executing code
A Trusted Platform Module that stores integrity measurements of the loaded software
Address space layout randomization applied to the kernel's memory regions at boot
A hardware security module that isolates cryptographic keys and operations from the host

q: A hospital issues thousands of laptops that routinely leave the campus. Leadership wants stored patient data protected if a device is lost or stolen, with negligible performance impact and no reliance on users to configure or enable anything. Which capability BEST meets these requirements?
c: File and folder encryption utilities that staff apply to documents they consider sensitive
Self-encrypting drives with pre-boot authentication, provisioned and managed centrally
A Trusted Platform Module that records boot measurements to support remote attestation
A mobile device management agent that can issue a remote wipe once a loss is reported

q: Analysts with legitimate access to an unclassified logistics database run broad queries and correlate shipment schedules, unit identifiers, and destination codes, deriving deployment details the organization treats as classified. Every individual field is releasable on its own. Which vulnerability does this illustrate, and what mitigates it?
c: A covert storage channel, mitigated by auditing shared file system objects for signaling behavior
An injection flaw, mitigated by parameterizing queries and validating all analyst-supplied input
Aggregation, mitigated by monitoring query patterns and limiting the combinations of records any one user can assemble
An inference gap in the multilevel database, mitigated by polyinstantiating the sensitive records at each level

q: A team migrates a batch workload to a cloud function-as-a-service platform and asserts that, because the provider patches the servers and manages the runtime, no application security work remains on their side. Which responsibility does the customer STILL retain in this model?
c: Patching the operating system images on the hosts that execute the functions
Ensuring physical security of the provider's data centers that run the platform
Hardening the hypervisor and maintaining isolation between platform tenants
Securing the function code, its third-party dependencies, and the permissions granted to each function

q: Forensics shows malware on retail point-of-sale terminals harvested cardholder data from process memory in the interval between card read and transmission. Disk encryption and TLS to the payment processor were both operating correctly. Which architectural change BEST mitigates this class of attack?
c: Negotiate stronger TLS cipher suites for all traffic sent to the payment processor
Adopt point-to-point encryption so card data is encrypted inside the tamper-resistant reader before it ever reaches terminal memory
Deploy full disk encryption with longer keys on every point-of-sale terminal
Push updated antivirus signatures to the point-of-sale fleet on a daily schedule

q: A company is terminating a cloud contract. Its regulated data resided on provider-managed storage that is replicated across facilities and eventually reallocated to other tenants, so the company can never degauss or physically destroy the media. Which approach gives the BEST assurance that the data cannot be recovered after departure?
c: Encrypt the data with customer-controlled keys throughout its life and destroy those keys at termination, rendering all remnants unreadable
Delete every object through the provider's console and confirm the recycle containers are emptied
Obtain a signed certificate of destruction from the provider covering all storage the tenant used
Overwrite the allocated storage volumes with multiple passes of random data before closing the account

q: A company needs roughly 200 external partners to exchange confidential documents, but maintaining a unique pre-shared symmetric key for every pair of parties has become unmanageable, requiring nearly 20,000 keys. Which approach BEST solves this scalability problem?
c: Issue one shared symmetric key that all partners use for every exchange
Increase the length of each symmetric key to strengthen the existing scheme
Adopt asymmetric cryptography so each party needs only one published public key and one private key
Rotate the existing pairwise symmetric keys on a much more frequent schedule

q: A regulator requires that database administrators be unable to view customers' account numbers. The DBA team argues that the transparent data encryption (TDE) already enabled on the database satisfies this requirement. Why is the security architect right to push back, and what should be used instead?
c: TDE uses outdated ciphers, so upgrading the database to a modern AES-256 configuration will satisfy the requirement
TDE protects only database backups, so extending it to cover the live datafiles will close the gap
TDE keys reside on the database server, so migrating them into a network HSM will stop administrators from reading data
TDE decrypts transparently for any authorized database session, so application-layer encryption with keys held outside the database is needed

q: A vendor signs software releases with a code-signing certificate valid for three years. Customers report that installers which verified correctly at release begin failing signature validation after the certificate expires, even though the packages are unchanged. What should the vendor add to its signing process?
c: A trusted timestamp from a timestamping authority proving each signature was created while the certificate was still valid
A procedure to re-sign every previously shipped release whenever a new signing certificate is issued
A ten-year code-signing certificate so that signatures outlast the supported life of the software
OCSP stapling so that verifiers receive fresh revocation status alongside each signed package

q: Threat intelligence indicates an adversary can obtain fraudulent yet technically valid TLS certificates for arbitrary domains from a compromised public certificate authority. A bank wants its mobile application's sessions protected even if such a certificate is presented to it. Which control BEST addresses this threat?
c: Require Extended Validation certificates for all of the bank's public-facing domains
Pin the server's expected certificate or public key in the app so connections presenting any other key are rejected
Shorten server certificate lifetimes and require revocation checking through OCSP
Enforce TLS 1.3 with only strong, modern cipher suites for every application session

q: An adversary obtains years of a company's encrypted archived reports and knows that every report begins with the same standard cover page and boilerplate legal text. The adversary lines up these known portions against the corresponding ciphertext to work toward recovering the key. Which cryptanalytic attack model is this?
c: Chosen-plaintext attack, because the attacker controls which text gets encrypted
Ciphertext-only attack, because the attacker's evidence is captured ciphertext
Known-plaintext attack, because the attacker holds plaintext-ciphertext pairs it did not choose
Chosen-ciphertext attack, because the attacker studies decryption of selected messages

q: A web service validates each API request's MAC with a routine that compares bytes sequentially and returns as soon as one byte mismatches. Researchers demonstrate that a remote attacker can forge a valid MAC by measuring response-time differences across many crafted guesses. Which attack class is this, and what is the appropriate fix?
c: A padding oracle attack, fixed by switching to an authenticated encryption mode
A birthday attack on the MAC, fixed by doubling the length of the MAC output
A replay attack on captured requests, fixed by adding nonces and timestamps
A timing side-channel attack, fixed by using a constant-time comparison routine

q: An attacker on a hotel's network records the encrypted 'unlock' exchange between a wireless door controller and its management server, then retransmits the identical ciphertext later and opens the door without decrypting or altering anything. Which attack occurred, and which countermeasure defeats it?
c: A replay attack, countered by a timestamp or single-use nonce that the controller validates before acting
A man-in-the-middle attack, countered by mutual authentication between controller and server
A brute-force key recovery attack, countered by moving to substantially longer encryption keys
A downgrade attack, countered by disabling the legacy cipher suites the protocol still accepts

q: A campus redesign adds low decorative fencing, distinctive pavement marking the transition from public sidewalk to company grounds, prominent corporate signage, and meticulously maintained landscaping, so visitors clearly perceive where private property begins and intruders feel conspicuous. Which CPTED strategy does this apply?
c: Natural surveillance, by ensuring occupants and passersby can observe activity on the grounds
Territorial reinforcement, by using design elements that express ownership and define private space
Natural access control, by funneling all pedestrian movement toward supervised entry points
Target hardening, by adding physical barriers that resist forced entry onto the property

q: During a data center walkthrough, an auditor notes that relative humidity in the equipment aisles has been holding near 20 percent for several months. Why is this reading a concern for the installed hardware?
c: It creates conditions for corrosion and rust to form on internal metal components
It indicates the space is being overcooled, which will cause processors to overheat
It increases the buildup and discharge of static electricity that can damage sensitive electronics
It promotes mold growth inside the facility's air handling and ductwork systems

q: A server room's raised floor conceals power distribution whips and the chilled-water lines that feed in-row cooling units. The facilities team asks what detective control should be installed in the underfloor plenum to address the specific risk this design introduces. Which control BEST fits?
c: Pre-action sprinkler heads positioned beneath the raised floor tiles
Positive air pressurization maintained throughout the underfloor plenum
Aspirating smoke detectors sampling air continuously from the plenum space
Moisture and leak detection sensors placed along the chilled-water piping runs

q: An operational system holding a current authorization is scheduled for a major software upgrade that changes its authentication flow. Under the organization's system lifecycle and configuration management process, what must occur FIRST before the change is approved for production?
c: A security impact analysis of the proposed change to determine its effect on the system's control posture
A complete reauthorization effort culminating in a new approval from the authorizing official
Decommissioning of the current system so the upgraded version can re-enter the lifecycle at initiation
A penetration test of the upgraded authentication functionality in the production environment

q: A fintech startup's platform team allows the same engineers to write application code, approve their own merge requests, and deploy directly to the production environment. An architecture review flags this workflow. Which secure design principle is MOST directly violated?
c: Least privilege, because engineers hold more system permissions than their daily tasks require
Defense in depth, because a single compromised workstation could affect production systems
Separation of duties, because no independent party must concur before a change reaches production
Economy of mechanism, because the deployment pipeline contains too many complex steps

q: In a multilevel system enforcing Bell-LaPadula, an administrator downgrades a document's label from Secret to Confidential while several Secret-cleared users still have it open, and the system permits the relabel without further checks. Which model concept does this operation put at risk?
c: The tranquility principle, which constrains changing security labels on active subjects and objects
The simple security property, which prevents subjects from reading objects above their clearance
The *-property, which prevents subjects from writing information into lower-classified objects
Discretionary access via the access matrix, which lets owners grant permissions to other subjects

q: An analyst merges extracts from two compartmented datasets — one labeled Secret//ALPHA and one labeled Secret//BRAVO — into a single report. Under a lattice-based access control model, what label must the combined report receive?
c: Secret with no compartments, since the compartment markings cancel out when data is merged
The least upper bound of the two labels, Secret//ALPHA,BRAVO, which dominates both sources
Top Secret, because combining compartments always raises the classification one level
The greatest lower bound of the two labels, so any reader of either compartment can access it

q: A new payroll application will run in the organization's existing data center, which already provides badge access, environmental monitoring, and fire suppression managed by the facilities team. When selecting the application's control baseline, how should the architect treat these physical and environmental controls?
c: Scope them out of the baseline as not applicable to an application-layer system
Re-implement them within the application project so the system owner controls them directly
Replace them with compensating controls documented in the application's security plan
Designate them as common controls inherited from the facility provider and document the inheritance

q: Executives travel with laptops that have external high-speed ports supporting direct memory access. A security assessment warns that an attacker with brief physical access could use a malicious peripheral to read encryption keys straight from RAM. Which platform capability BEST addresses this threat?
c: Enabling the input-output memory management unit to restrict peripheral access to system memory
Turning on full-disk encryption so data stored on the drive remains protected
Enforcing data execution prevention so injected code pages cannot run
Requiring a BIOS/UEFI password so firmware settings cannot be changed

q: A cloud-hosted web application fetches preview images from user-supplied URLs. A penetration test shows the feature can be pointed at the cloud provider's instance metadata endpoint, returning temporary credentials for the server's role. Which remediation BEST addresses the architectural weakness?
c: Deploy a web application firewall with signatures that block known malicious inbound payloads
Encrypt the application's data stores so stolen credentials cannot expose readable records
Require session-oriented, hop-limited metadata requests and restrict the fetcher's outbound destinations to an allow-list
Rotate the exposed role credentials immediately and shorten their validity period going forward

q: Employees increasingly read corporate email and documents on personally owned phones. Legal objects to seizing or fully wiping personal devices, while security worries about corporate data leaking through personal apps and cloud backups. Which approach BEST balances these concerns?
c: Prohibit all corporate data access from personally owned devices until company phones are issued
Deploy managed containers that isolate corporate apps and data and support selective wipe of only the work profile
Require full-device enrollment giving the organization remote wipe over the entire handset
Mandate VPN connections from personal devices so traffic to corporate services is encrypted

q: On a shared server, a low-privilege process is observed inferring data from a sensitive partition it cannot read. Investigation shows a cooperating high-side process varies its CPU consumption in a coded rhythm that the low-side process measures through system responsiveness. No shared files or memory are involved. What has been discovered?
c: A covert storage channel, because the CPU scheduler is being used as a shared writable object
A side-channel attack, because the receiver passively exploits unintended physical leakage
Steganography, because the message is hidden inside apparently innocent system activity
A covert timing channel, because information is signaled through modulation of observable timing behavior

q: An engineer proposes that remote telemetry units establish session keys with the control server using anonymous Diffie-Hellman, arguing that the exchange never transmits the secret key over the network. What is the MOST significant weakness of this design?
c: An active on-path attacker can substitute their own parameters and establish separate keys with each side
The shared secret is transmitted in a recoverable form during the exchange
Diffie-Hellman keys are inherently too short to resist modern brute-force attacks
Captured sessions can be replayed later to issue duplicate control commands

q: A storage platform holds hundreds of millions of encrypted objects, each encrypted under its own data key. Policy requires the ability to rotate cryptographic material regularly without re-processing petabytes of stored data. Which key architecture BEST satisfies the requirement?
c: Extend the cryptoperiod of a single storage key so that rotation is needed less frequently
Wrap each object's data key with a master key-encrypting key, so rotation re-wraps the small key records instead of the data
Re-encrypt the full object store with a fresh key at every scheduled rotation window
Derive every object's key on demand from a static passphrase combined with the object identifier

q: Outside counsel must exchange privileged case files with the legal department by email. Messages traverse several intermediate mail relays operated by third parties. Which solution BEST protects the confidentiality of message content across the full path?
c: Enforce TLS on every server-to-server mail connection along the route
Sign all outgoing messages with the organization's domain keys
Encrypt messages end-to-end with S/MIME using the recipients' certificates
Store mailbox databases on encrypted volumes at both organizations

q: Researchers find that thousands of a vendor's network appliances share factorable TLS private keys. Analysis shows each unit generated its key pair automatically within seconds of its very first power-on. What is the MOST likely root cause?
c: The chosen key length is too small for the algorithm to resist factoring
The appliances default to a weak export-grade cipher suite during the handshake
A hash collision during certificate issuance produced duplicate key material
Key generation drew from an entropy pool that was barely seeded at first boot

q: A laptop in sleep mode is stolen from a conference room. Forensic reconstruction shows the thief chilled the memory modules, force-restarted the machine into a minimal operating system from USB, and dumped RAM contents to recover the full-disk encryption key. Which attack does this describe?
c: A cold boot attack exploiting DRAM data remanence after power interruption
An evil maid attack that tampers with the bootloader to capture credentials
A power-analysis side channel measuring consumption during decryption
A brute-force attack against the pre-boot authentication password

q: A cryptanalyst attacks a block cipher by submitting large numbers of chosen plaintext pairs that differ in carefully selected bit positions, then studies how those input differences propagate through the rounds into statistical patterns in the ciphertext. Which technique is being applied?
c: Linear cryptanalysis, approximating the cipher's behavior with probable linear equations
Differential cryptanalysis, tracing the propagation of controlled input differences
Frequency analysis, matching ciphertext symbol distributions to language statistics
A meet-in-the-middle attack, computing forward and backward to a common intermediate state

q: A legacy API authenticates requests with a tag computed as Hash(secret || message) using an iterated Merkle-Damgard hash. A tester demonstrates forging valid tags for messages with attacker-chosen data appended, without ever learning the secret. Which weakness enables this, and what fixes it?
c: Weak collision resistance of the digest; move to a hash with a larger output size
Predictable secrets; enforce longer keys so tags cannot be guessed
Length extension of the secret-prefix construction; replace it with HMAC's nested keyed design
Missing transport protection; wrap the API in TLS so tags cannot be observed

q: A facility assessment finds that couriers delivering packages walk through the main operations corridor, passing the network operations center and an unlocked storage room, to reach a receiving desk deep inside the building. Which redesign BEST addresses the exposure?
c: Install additional cameras along the corridor to record all delivery traffic
Require couriers to sign a visitor log and wear temporary badges while inside
Run background screening on the courier companies' delivery personnel
Relocate receiving to a segregated dock area with a controlled hand-off point at the building edge

q: A company builds a new primary data center beside a highway and plans large exterior signs carrying the company logo and the words 'National Data Center.' From a facility security standpoint, what is the BEST guidance?
c: Omit signs identifying the building's purpose, keeping the facility deliberately low-profile
Keep the signs, since visible ownership markings provide territorial reinforcement
Keep the signs, because hiding a facility's purpose is security through obscurity, which adds no value
Replace the signs with warning placards describing prosecution for trespassing

q: In a headquarters building, any employee badge that opens the lobby turnstiles also opens every interior door, including the server room and the executive records vault. Which design change BEST corrects this weakness?
c: Upgrade the perimeter with taller fencing and additional exterior guard patrols
Establish concentric security zones with progressively stricter access as spaces become more sensitive
Add cameras covering the server room and vault doors with motion-triggered recording
Issue visitor badges in a distinct color so staff can challenge unfamiliar persons

q: A distribution company must add sprinkler coverage to an unheated loading dock and attached storage bay in a region with sub-freezing winters. Which suppression design is MOST appropriate?
c: A wet-pipe system, because water at every head gives the fastest possible discharge
A deluge system, so all heads flood the area at once when smoke is detected
A dry-pipe system, keeping pipes charged with air until a head activates
A pre-action system, requiring both detection and head activation before water flows

q: During a walkthrough, an assessor finds that the telecommunications closets on each floor are unlocked and double as storage for cleaning supplies, with switches and patch panels openly accessible. What is the BEST corrective action?
c: Encrypt all network traffic so physical access to the switches yields nothing useful
Mount cameras in the corridors outside each closet to record who enters
Label all cabling and patch panels so unauthorized changes are easier to spot
